disambiguation_summary.verdict: c150 is the operational champion — only precision-clean checkpoint on new-venue goals (0 FP), preserves rush baseline (F1 0.519, goal P/R 0.50/0.50). c50 has +0.004 agg F1 lift but costs 4 goal FPs. c200 regresses on rush. All within FP8 noise on agg F1.
disambiguation_summary.key_finding: v10's trajectory-aware training plateaued at c150. New-venue goal recall is 1/16 across ALL checkpoints. More training (c200) doesn't help; less training (c50) loses goal precision. Coordinate-based trajectory features have hit their ceiling.
disambiguation_summary.eval_loss_misleading: c50 had lowest eval_loss (0.10199) but matched c150's F1, while c200 (0.10386, more training) underperformed both. Token-level CE doesn't track event-classification F1.

recommended_next_steps.name: Hybrid v10 c150 + v8 portfolio
recommended_next_steps.rationale: Ship the precision win immediately. Route goal/save events through c150 (0 FP new-venue goals, 1.00 P on game_20), everything else through v8 (better recall on majority classes). Captures the iteration signal without any new training.

recommended_next_steps.name: v11 LoRA with velocity/acceleration trajectory features
recommended_next_steps.rationale: Coordinate-based trajectory has plateaued. Velocity (Δ/frame) and acceleration (Δ²/frame) compress trajectory into shape primitives that may be easier for the LLM to parse than raw (x,y). Goal-vs-shot is mostly an acceleration-profile question.

recommended_next_steps.name: v11 with longer schedule + lower LR (deprioritized)
recommended_next_steps.rationale: Run 85/89/93 results suggest the model has already learned what coordinate trajectories can teach. More steps of the same recipe will not break the new-venue goal-recall plateau.
